notes: Control of Hypertension In Pregnancy Study. Non-severe HTN in pregnancy. Tight control: NO harm to baby, reduced maternal severe HTN (27.5% vs 40.6%, p<0.001). Safe and beneficial.

Hypertension and Pre-eclampsia Intervention Trial At Term. Mild gestational HTN/PE ≥36 weeks. Induction reduced maternal adverse outcomes (31% vs 44%, p<0.01). No increase in C-section. Induction beneficial.
Aspirin for Evidence-Based Preeclampsia Prevention. High-risk women. Aspirin reduced preterm PE 62% (1.6% vs 4.3%, p<0.001). Game-changer for PE prevention. Early + high-dose key.
Magpie Trial predecessor. Eclampsia management. MgSO4 reduced recurrent seizures 59% (3.6% vs 8.8%) and maternal death 46%. Established MgSO4 as standard for eclampsia.
Pre-eclampsia prevention of eclampsia. MgSO4 reduced eclampsia 58% (0.8% vs 1.9%, p<0.001). Saved lives. Largest PE trial ever. WHO essential medicine.

Management of Myelomeningocele Study. Maternal cardiac stress from fetal surgery. Prenatal surgery: increased maternal complications but improved child outcomes. Risk-benefit in maternal-fetal medicine.
Severe hypertensive episodes in pregnancy/postpartum. IV labetalol faster BP control, fewer persistent severe HTN (12.5% vs 23.3%, p=0.03). IV preferred for acute severe HTN in pregnancy.
